title: the band room Rising
premise: Jonah Iversen counts the days to graduation at Hollow Creek High, a school built over a flooded band hall where, decades ago, a marching band drowned during a storm. When a group chat called 'the band room' begins predicting deaths before they happen, Jonah and four classmates realize they've been drafted into a bargain: win the state championship that no one cares about — and the older, stranger contest beneath it — or the school will collect them one by one. As predictions come true and memories surface that aren't theirs, Jonah falls for Priya, whose grandmother was in the original band, and learns love is the only thing the room can't count. In the end they play the unfinished piece from 1974 at the championship, giving the drowned their ending; Priya nearly joins them, but Jonah's refusal to let go breaks the cycle, and the group chat goes silent forever.
about_author: Mara Dunmore is a former high school music teacher who spent six years in a building with a basement nobody would explain. She writes stories about teenagers who notice what adults have agreed to forget.

chapters.title: Day One Hundred and Twelve
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. He narrates his countdown calendar at Hollow Creek High, establishing his detachment and the school's odd architecture — the band room that's warmer than it should be, doors that hum. Emotional beat: numb survival, until a group chat invite arrives from numbers he doesn't know.

chapters.title: The Chat That Knew
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The chat predicts a pipe burst in the gym — it happens within the hour. Members include Priya, skeptical Marcus, anxious Wren, and quiet Dev. Emotional beat: uncanny dread masked by teenage sarcasm.

chapters.title: Basement Acoustics
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. She drags Jonah to the sealed sub-basement under the band room, where water stains rise up the walls like a tide line. Her grandmother's old sheet music is nailed to a beam. Emotional beat: fascination curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Second Prediction
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The chat names a janitor's accident two days early; Wren tries to warn him and fails. The group realizes warnings don't work — only participation does. Emotional beat: guilt as a first taste of the price.

chapters.title: Counting Backwards
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Research montage: the 1974 flood, the lost marching band, a trophy case photo where faces are water-blurred. Jonah recognizes his own posture in one blurred figure. Emotional beat: the countdown calendar starts feeling like someone else's handwriting.

chapters.title: Audition
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. The chat issues its first demand: all five must join band and compete at regionals. Marcus, a drummer who quit after his brother's death, refuses — and that night hears snare rolls inside his walls. Emotional beat: grief weaponized.

chapters.title: Priya's Grandmother
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Visiting her grandmother, she finds a diary describing 'the second contest' — a championship played for the drowned, judged by something in the water. Grandma begs her to drop out. Emotional beat: inherited duty versus inherited love.

chapters.title: Regionals
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. They perform badly on purpose, hoping to be eliminated; instead the judges score them impossibly high, and the chat posts tomorrow's date with a name: Wren's. Emotional beat: winning feels like losing.

chapters.title: What Wren Saw
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren follows the sound of a tuba into the flooded sub-basement and sees the 1974 band standing in ankle-deep water, still playing. She comes back changed, speaking in fragments. Emotional beat: awe breaking a person open.

chapters.title: Saving Wren
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The group tries everything to break Wren's prediction — hiding her, driving out of county lines. The chat simply moves the deadline. Emotional beat: the futility of running, and Jonah's first real choice to stay.

chapters.title: First Kiss, Last Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Late rehearsal turns into an almost-confession between Jonah and Priya; the room's temperature drops, jealous. They kiss anyway. Emotional beat: love chosen deliberately inside a trap.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus discovers the contest's rule: the room will accept a substitute — anyone who volunteers willingly. His brother's old drumsticks feel like an answer. Emotional beat: sacrificial logic seducing a grieving boy.

chapters.title: Interruption
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah catches Marcus mid-ritual in the sub-basement and pulls him back; the water rises an inch in anger. The five finally pool everything they know. Emotional beat: solidarity forged in near-loss.

chapters.title: The Unfinished Piece
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The diary reveals the 1974 band died mid-song — their competition piece has no final movement. Winning means finishing it. Priya transcribes her grandmother's sketches while the chat counts down to state finals. Emotional beat: hope with a deadline.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. A rival school's director, whose father survived '74 by abandoning the band, tries to get them disqualified. Dev, the quiet one, blackmails him with the truth. Emotional beat: moral compromise in service of survival.

chapters.title: Wren's Deadline
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. On her predicted day, Wren walks toward the water voluntarily, serene. The others play the unfinished movement outside the sealed door — and the chat glitches, postponing her date. Emotional beat: the first proof the rules can bend.

chapters.title: State Finals
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Championship day: a real crowd, real stakes that don't matter, and the sub-basement flooding upward through the gym floor as the true judges arrive. Emotional beat: terror braided with performance adrenaline.

chapters.title: The Second Contest
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Mid-performance, the gym becomes the flooded hall of 1974. The drowned band plays opposite them, note for note. Priya's grandmother appears among them, young again, holding out a hand. Emotional beat: love against duty at full volume.

chapters.title: Final Movement
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. They play the completed finale; the drowned begin to fade, released. But the room demands a closer — Priya, whose bloodline started the bargain. Emotional beat: the climax's terrible arithmetic.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah steps between Priya and the water and refuses to count anything — days, debts, lives. He plays off-sheet, off-rules, human and imperfect, and the judging silence cracks. Emotional beat: defiance as grace.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The water recedes; the sub-basement is dry for the first time since 1974. Wren returns to herself, Marcus keeps playing, and the group chat sends one last message: 'thank you.' Emotional beat: exhausted tenderness.

chapters.title: Day Zero
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Graduation day. Jonah crosses the stage without counting, then tears up the countdown calendar in the empty band room, which is just a room now. He and Priya walk out together. Emotional beat: time returned, memory kept, survival finally free.
